apps/web/src/features/README.md.content:
# Features

One folder per feature, e.g. `src/features/reading-list/`. Each has one public entry,
`index.ts`; other code imports only that file, and only if `docs/app/modules.json` allows it.
`fwos check walls` enforces both.

A feature usually holds: `components/` (views built from `@/shared/ui`), `data/` (a repository that
matches the API contract, so mock, local and real backends swap), `model/` (logic, no UI), and tests
named with the AC they prove (`@AC-<feature>-<n>`).

apps/web/tsconfig.json.content:
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "lib": ["dom", "dom.iterable", "esnext"],
    "allowJs": false,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "module": "esnext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "incremental": true,
    "plugins": [{ "name": "next" }],
    "paths": { "@/*": ["./src/*"] },
    "types": ["vitest/globals", "@testing-library/jest-dom"]
  },
  "include": ["next-env.d.ts", "**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", ".next/types/**/*.ts", ".next/dev/types/**/*.ts"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules"]
}

packages/api-contract/openapi.yaml.content:
# The API contract. The architecture step fills in paths; fixtures go in fixtures/ as
# <operationId>.<variant>.json holding { "status": 200, "body": ... }. `fwos contract mocks`
# turns them into a fail-closed mock fetch, and `fwos check` validates every fixture here.
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: "Gallery sample API"
  version: 0.1.0
paths: {}
components:
  schemas: {}
